overview: The Medford City Council tabled the proposed FY16 municipal budget pending overdue account transfer reports from the administration. The council also addressed Eversource transmission line plans, cable franchise negotiations, environmental mandates, and school policies.

items.title: MBTA West Medford Commuter Rail Station cleanup
items.summary: Approved a resolution as amended requesting the MBTA conduct a spring cleanup at the West Medford station and encase an on-site portable toilet.

items.title: Electronic cigarette regulation
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting the Board of Health propose a draft ordinance regulating the sale and use of electronic cigarettes in Medford.

items.title: Eversource underground transmission line project
items.summary: Approved questions and mitigation inquiries for Eversource representatives regarding their proposed 3.2-mile underground electrical transmission line through Medford ahead of a presentation next week.

items.title: School surveys and House Bill 283
items.summary: Failed a motion to endorse the intent of state legislation requiring written parental consent for sensitive school health surveys after debate over parental rights and the presenting group.

items.title: Medford Public Library budget and accreditation
items.summary: Approved a motion requesting the library director present a five-year plan and report during upcoming budget hearings on the funding required to preserve state accreditation and Minuteman network access.

items.title: Commendation of Richard Cormier
items.summary: Presented a resolution congratulating paramedic and council videographer Richard Cormier on receiving the American Ambulance Association's Stars of Life Award.

items.title: Licenses and taxi vehicle transfers
items.summary: Approved vehicle exchanges for Metro Transit and Mystic Cab, and granted a common victualler license to Medford Square Diner.

items.title: Oak Grove Cemetery mausoleum proposal
items.summary: Approved a request to meet with the Board of Cemetery Trustees following their June meeting to discuss proposals to construct a public mausoleum at Oak Grove Cemetery.

items.title: Comcast franchise ascertainment and contract renewal
items.summary: Approved motions directing residents to submit comments to the mayor by May 21 regarding the Comcast cable contract and reaffirming prior resolutions against a 10-year agreement.

items.title: EPA MS4 stormwater sewer permit mandate
items.summary: Approved a resolution petitioning regulatory agencies to defer and extend deadlines on proposed unfunded federal stormwater permit requirements.

items.title: Tabling of FY16 municipal budget
items.summary: Tabled the FY16 municipal budget submission due to the administration's failure to provide requested accounting reports on municipal fund transfers.

items.title: Sidewalk audit and street maintenance
items.summary: Approved an inquiry to the Department of Public Works regarding the status of a sidewalk assessment and the planned use of state winter infrastructure funds.

items.title: Citizen petition on community policing
items.summary: Placed on file a citizen petition outlining proposals for community policing reforms, volunteer community advocates, and restorative justice measures.

items.title: Police patrol vehicle fleet updates
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting that the mayor update the city's police patrol fleet with new cruisers.

items.title: High school NEASC accreditation and vocational programs
items.summary: Approved a resolution congratulating high school and vocational school staff for earning a 10-year NEASC accreditation, while requesting an administrative report regarding rumored vocational program restructuring.

items.title: West Medford parking lot contamination
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting that environmental, engineering, and community development officials appear before the council to provide an update on remediation plans for the contaminated West Medford lot.

items.title: Approval of minutes
items.summary: Approved the records of the April 20 and May 5, 2015 meetings.
